symbols.name: triple S
symbols.meaning: A three-element subset of the ground set, called a triple, paired with T as a candidate neighbor.
symbols.quote: Here $S$ and $T$ denote three-element subsets of $[h]$, called triples; on earlier pages these letters denote other objects.

symbols.name: triple T
symbols.meaning: A three-element subset of the ground set, called a triple, whose indicator vector is discussed.
symbols.quote: Here $S$ and $T$ denote three-element subsets of $[h]$, called triples; on earlier pages these letters denote other objects.

symbols.name: indicator vector of T
symbols.meaning: The 0-1 vector with an entry 1 in each position of T and 0 elsewhere.
symbols.quote: Its indicator vector $t_T$ has an entry $1$ in each position $e \in T$ and $0$ in every other position.

symbols.name: all-ones matrix
symbols.meaning: The h by h matrix with every entry equal to 1.
symbols.quote: Let $J$ be the $h\times h$ matrix of all ones.

symbols.name: binary field
symbols.meaning: The field with two elements, 0 and 1, in which 1+1=0.
symbols.quote: The complex construction uses the binary field $\mathbb{F}_2$, the field with two elements $0$ and $1$ with $1+1=0$, so its label field is $\mathbb{F}_2^h$

symbols.name: rational numbers
symbols.quote: Here $\mathbb{Q}$ denotes the rational numbers, not the ring $Q$ of an earlier page.

relations.quote: An indicator vector is the 0-1 vector that marks which elements of a [Ground set](ground-set.md) belong to a given subset.
